answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. This works because the originality bar tightens as more low-quality answers appear, raising the per-alias cost of a coordinated fake campaign. This design turns the attacker's greatest weapon — scale — into its weakest point, because scale is exactly what becomes unaffordable to maintain. Consider a marble as the anchor of the cost.
